**Q4.** A signed-in user's upload is received by `POST /api/v1/files/` (`upload_file`, `backend/open_webui/routers/files.py:271-312`), gated by `Depends(get_verified_user)` at `files.py:279`. The handler delegates to `upload_file_handler` (`files.py:315`), which reads the multipart bytes and calls `Storage.upload_file(file.file, filename, tags)` at `files.py:366`. With the default `local` storage provider, that resolves to `LocalStorageProvider.upload_file` (`backend/open_webui/storage/provider.py:59-67`), which reads the full contents and writes them with `open(file_path, 'wb').write(contents)` to `os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, filename)` (`provider.py:64-66`), where `filename` is `f'{id}_{filename}'` (`files.py:356-358`) — so the bytes land on local disk under `UPLOAD_DIR` (backend `data/uploads` by default) keyed by a generated UUID. A `File` row is then inserted via `Files.insert_new_file` (`files.py:399-419`), recording the path, content-type, size, and SHA-256 hash.

If `process=True` (the default, `files.py:277`), the upload also triggers content processing: either as a background task via `background_tasks.add_task(process_uploaded_file, ...)` (`files.py:427-436`) or inline (`files.py:439-447`). `process_uploaded_file` (`files.py:128-268`) branches on content type — audio/STT-supported files get transcribed via `transcribe(...)` (`files.py:155-160`) and then indexed, image/video files are either skipped or stored as-is (`files.py:168-187`), and everything else goes through `process_file` in `backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py:1837`, which extracts/chunks the document and writes it into the vector DB collection `file-{file.id}` via `ASYNC_VECTOR_DB_CLIENT` for retrieval-augmented search. If the upload's metadata carries a `knowledge_id`, it's also auto-linked into that Knowledge Collection after a write-access check (`files.py:204-247`). Finally, back in `upload_file`, an `EVENTS.FILE_UPLOADED` event is published with the filename and content type (`files.py:305-311`), and if `channel_id` was supplied in metadata the file is attached to that channel (`files.py:421-424`).
